items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: when we were 18, that when they heard the Glenn Miller band or a Charlie Barnet or a Count Basie or a Duke Ellington, they went crazy.

ctx.x: Can you put this in perspective for me a little bit? The music that you were playing at that time, what was the average age of the audience that would come to see you?

The audience? I’d say anywhere from 18 to 25, 30, somewhere around there. They were young kids. You know this is something that you mention, funny you mention that because I keep thinking about the fact that the music that we loved then, excuse me, with the big band, it was like jazz tinged. Everything was jazz flavored. Nowadays they’ve got these 18 year old kids, listening to rap or whatever other stuff they’re listening to, and I say what happened to these kids, when we were 18, that when they heard the Glenn…
That was the popular music of the day, what you were playing.
